current.text: Washington added Trae Young, Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa, all of whom missed last season.
Experts expect him to start, but it is not guaranteed. If he starts, he is likely the fifth offensive option.
Washington has a deep group of wings and guards, and the fifth starter spot is open.
Last season he played like a top 50 player for about two months while handling the ball more. His role then shrank and his production fell off badly.
Experts do not expect him to repeat last season's jump, because Young, Davis and Dybantsa will take usage from him. One expert called his efficiency last season horrific.
One expert puts him in tier 8 of small forwards. Another calls his ADP of 112 marginally high.
Ben thinks the organization likes him most of its young wings and guards, and sees him as the best all-around player in that group.
A trade of Anthony Davis would help his role. One expert is about 80% sure the Wizards keep Davis.
Washington is trying to compete for the play-in, so the late-season rest and minutes cuts of past years should not happen.

durable.text: He is a two-way wing who can guard shooting guard through power forward. He can struggle against quicker guards.
He shoots well from outside, especially on catch-and-shoot chances.
His blocks are good for a wing.
An arm injury ended his 2025-26 season early.

note: Yahoo and ESPN both price him at 1 USD, with ranks of 119 and 126. That puts him near the bottom of our 144-player draft, and he went for 2 USD in our league last season. His projected line is broad but thin: no category is weak, but FG% and TO are soft (z -0.9 each). Experts see his role shrinking next to Young, Davis and Dybantsa, so take him only as a 1 USD end-of-draft filler. In the first weeks, check whether he starts and whether his roughly 4 assists per game hold up.
